title: Argentina–France
provenance: Transcript and evidence from the saved argfra-openai-claude-v2 plan. Audio timings from the ElevenLabs render report.

lines.text: Argentina work the ball out from their own area.
France squeeze high, forcing that ball over the touchline.
Theo Hernández takes the throw into the left channel.
Argentina crowd it out inside the area.
That intervention flips possession into open midfield.
Driven forward to the near side.
Goal! Struck in from the left, past the goalkeeper!
End to end, finished first time.
France, ranked fourth entering the final, undone on the counter.

observations.description: A striped-shirt defender controls the ball inside his own penalty area as navy-shirt opponents press higher up the pitch.
The defender passes out of the penalty area toward a teammate near the near-side touchline.
Number 26 moves onto the bouncing pass outside the penalty area, near the touchline, as a navy-shirt opponent closes him down.
After the striped-shirt player's attempted touch, the ball goes out across the near touchline. The referee signals a direction; the final contact is not clear.
Navy-shirted number 22 holds the ball at the near touchline, preparing a throw-in.
Number 22 completes the throw-in; the following wide view shows the ball dropping toward a navy-shirted teammate outside the left side of the penalty area.
The navy-shirted receiver brings the ball near his feet outside the penalty area as two striped defenders close him down.
The navy-shirted attacker continues toward the left edge of the penalty area among converging striped defenders. The ball is obscured, so the next touch or possession is unclear.

Inside the left side of the penalty area, a navy-shirted attacker is challenged by a striped defender. The ball travels inward toward another striped defender; the touch that sends it there is unclear.
Following a striped defender's intervention, the ball is visibly high in the air, travelling away from the penalty area toward the near-side midfield channel.
A navy-shirted player receives the dropping ball near the near touchline, short of halfway, as a striped opponent approaches.
The navy-shirted ball carrier moves along the near touchline with the ball at his feet while the striped opponent closes to challenge.
The ball travels airborne infield from a near-touchline challenge between a navy-shirted player and a striped player, outside the penalty area; the final touch is unclear.
A striped player outside his own penalty area sends the ball diagonally infield toward teammates as navy-shirted opponents press.
The ball moves forward through central midfield toward a striped teammate short of halfway, with a navy-shirted opponent closing from his right.
Under pressure from two navy-shirted opponents, the striped receiver moves the ball diagonally forward toward a teammate running along the near side.
The near-side striped runner reaches the ball and advances across halfway as navy-shirted defenders retreat; the ball is briefly obscured near his feet.
Striped No. 9 runs forward during the attack. The close-up does not show the ball.
A forward ball travels into open space beyond midfield, with a striped attacker sprinting after it and navy defenders retreating.
The striped runner closes on the ball just outside the right side of the penalty area, with defenders pursuing and the goalkeeper facing him.
The right-side attacker sends the ball diagonally across the penalty area toward a striped teammate arriving from the left.
The arriving striped attacker shoots from inside the penalty area as the yellow-clad goalkeeper rushes out and spreads himself.
The ball is visible inside the right side of the net after passing the goalkeeper, who is down on the turf.
A striped-shirt attacker runs away along the byline as teammates spread their arms. The yellow-clad goalkeeper remains on the ground near the goal.
A close-up shows the striped-shirt player with 'DI MARIA' and number 11 readable on his back running in celebration.
The home player with shirt number 11 celebrates with arms spread and mouth open as a teammate approaches.
The camera cuts to supporters in white and sky-blue shirts raising their arms, waving flags and embracing in the stands.

research.subject: Argentina vs France
research.text: Pre-final head-to-head between the senior national teams stood at 12 meetings since 1930: Argentina six wins, France three wins, three draws (all competitions).

research.subject: Rankings
research.text: Entering the final, Argentina were ranked 3rd and France 4th in the FIFA world rankings.

research.subject: Venue and kickoff
research.text: The final was scheduled for Sunday 18 December 2022 at Lusail Iconic Stadium, Doha, kicking off at 18:00 local time (15:00 GMT).

research.subject: World Cup head-to-head
research.text: Before the 2022 final the sides had met three times at World Cups, with Argentina winning two; France's only World Cup win over Argentina was the 4-3 round-of-16 tie in 2018.

research.subject: Route to the final
research.text: Argentina reached the final by beating Croatia 3-0 in the semi-final on 13 December 2022, after a 2-1 win over Australia (R16) and a penalty-shootout win over the Netherlands (QF).

research.subject: Route to the final
research.text: Defending champions France reached the final via a 2-0 semi-final win over Morocco on 14 December 2022, having beaten England 2-1 in the quarter-final and Poland 3-1 in the round of 16.
